The probability of failure is the normalizing constant of the failure distribution!

In this lecture, we will discuss ways to estimate it.

An estimator is unbiased if it
predicts the true value in
expectation:
E[p^​fail​]=pfail​
An estimator is consistent if it
converges to the true value in
the limit of infinite samples:
m→∞lim​p^​fail​=pfail​
The variance of an estimator
quantifies the spread of the
estimates around the true value.

Again, bad news for systems with rare failure events.
We will discuss importance sampling techniques
throughout the rest of this lecture that aim to
address this issue!
Direct Estimation
But first: one more issue with maximum likelihood estimation.
Imagine that we want to estimate the probability of failure for an aircraft collision avoidance system
from an aviation safety database that contains flight records from the month of December.
What would the maximum likelihood estimate of the probability of failure be if there were no
recorded midair collisions in December?
Zero!
We could use Bayesian estimation in this case to produce a distribution over the probability of failure.

Importance Sampling
Is there an optimal proposal distribution?
We will define the optimal proposal
distribution as the one that minimizes the
variance of the estimator:
Var[p^​fail​]=m1​Eτ∼q(⋅)​[q(τ)(p(τ)1{τ∈/ψ}−q(τ)pfail​)2​]
Importance Sampling
Is there an optimal proposal distribution?
We will define the optimal proposal
distribution as the one that minimizes the
variance of the estimator:
Var[p^​fail​]=m1​Eτ∼q(⋅)​[q(τ)(p(τ)1{τ∈/ψ}−q(τ)pfail​)2​]
q∗(τ)=pfail​p(τ)1{τ∈/ψ}​
Does this distribution look familiar?
It’s the failure distribution!
🤔…but it is written in terms of the
thing we want to estimate (pfail​).

the proposal distribution we choose.
Various importance sampling algorithms have different ways of selecting this proposal.
One option: hand design based on domain knowledge.

Cross Entropy Method
What if we could still fit a good proposal using samples from
a different distribution that is easier to sample from?
1
Draw samples from an initial proposal distribution that is easy sample from.
2
Use the samples to fit a new proposal distribution from a model class that we also know how
to sample from by selecting the parameters that minimize the cross entropy between the
proposal distribution and the failure distribution.
Cross Entropy Method
What if we could still fit a good proposal using samples from
a different distribution that is easier to sample from?
1
Draw samples from an initial proposal distribution that is easy sample from.
τ∼q(⋅)
What proposal distribution should we try?
How about the nominal trajectory distribution?
2
Use the samples to fit a new proposal distribution from a model class that we also know how
to sample from by selecting the parameters that minimize the cross entropy between the
proposal distribution and the failure distribution.
For many common model classes (e.g. Gaussian), minimizing the cross entropy is equivalent
to computing the weighted maximum likelihood estimate for the parameters with weights
w=q(τ)p(τ)1{τ∈/ψ}​
Cross Entropy Method
If we sample from the nominal distribution and failures are rare,
we may not get any failures and all the weights will be zero!

We typically move the samples through a series of intermediate distributions.
How can we get these intermediate distributions? SMOOTHING!

Sequential Monte Carlo
We want to move samples from the nominal distribution to the failure distribution.
We typically move the samples through a series of intermediate distributions.
How can we get these intermediate distributions? SMOOTHING!
We can also use the thresholding technique similar to
what we did for the cross entropy method.
Sequential Monte Carlo
We want to move samples from the nominal distribution to the failure distribution.
We typically move the samples through a series of intermediate distributions.
How can we get these intermediate distributions? SMOOTHING!
We can also use the thresholding technique similar to
what we did for the cross entropy method.
How do we move samples from one distribution to the next? MCMC!

Sequential Monte Carlo
A few other notes on SMC:
It is common to also do a resampling step similar to population Monte Carlo for each transition.
Example 7.6
This process may allow us to perform fewer MCMC steps.
SMC is nonparametric, we do everything with samples.
This feature allows it to perform well for complex, multimodal failure distributions.

the ratio of the normalizing constants of two distributions.
